newsitem.title: USA: Strong earnings spark oil services stock rally.
newsitem.headline: Strong earnings spark oil services stock rally.

text.p: Shares of oil services companies rallied Thursday after strong earnings from key companies sparked optimism for the sector, analysts said.

"We've seen a sharp pullback the last couple of days. Investors were worried that the sector may be running out of steam. But the earnings have shown that it's not slowing," said John Lavoi, an analyst with Morgan Stanley.
Earnings momentum is expected to build in the near term as companies benefit from 1997 pricing increases, analysts said.
Halliburton Co posted fourth-quarter earnings of $0.85 a share on revenues of $1.99 billion, up from earnings of $0.63 a share on revenues of $1.58 billion. Halliburton gained 3-5/8 to 72-1/2.
Morgan upgraded Halliburton to outperform from neutral and reiterated strong buy ratings on Schlumberger Ltd and Baker Hughes Inc. Salomon Brothers also upgraded Halliburton and Baker Hughes.
Baker Hughes, which makes oil well drilling bits, gained 1-1/2 to 38-1/8. The company posted first quarter operating earnings of $0.35 a share, compared to $0.23 a share last year.
Analysts said the bellwether company's strong earnings sparked optimism that Cooper Cameron Corp would also top expectations.

Cooper Cameron, which has consistently outperformed Wall Street estimates in the past few quarters, is expected to earn $0.89 a share in the fourth quarter, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.
